doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Out of Nowhere: a radio hit that never sold
summary: The record got heavy airplay and jukebox plays but MGM said it had not sold.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And you had a big hit with that band Out of Nowhere that got a lot of radio play, right?
Oh, it really wasn’t a hit.

But it got a lot of radio play, in fact, we thought it was a hit. And Lenny then called MGM and said, “You know, what about the royalties on it.” And they said, “What royalties? You’ve got nothing coming, it’s not selling.” But we heard it on jukeboxes and we heard it on radio.

Nobody knows, nobody knows. I thought for sure it was a hit because of the exposure it got. But when they showed us the money, you know, the results and on paper it did nothing, it was dismal. So I don’t know.
And it wasn’t that all the royalties went to Lenny?
No, not really, I don’t think so. I think that it just was a turntable hit, as they called it in those days.
It really didn’t amount to real sales and a real hit.
